title: Openness of bounded local fibre dimension on the source
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $s\in S$ let $X_s$ be its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For $x\in X$, let $\widetilde x$ be the unique point of $X_{f(x)}$ mapping to $x$ under its projection to $X$, and let $\dim_{\widetilde x}X_{f(x)}$ be the topological dimension at that point [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], namely the minimum of the Krull dimensions of its open neighbourhoods in the fibre. For every integer $n\geq0$, the subset $$U_n=\{x\in X\mid\dim_{\widetilde x}X_{f(x)}\leq n\}$$ is open in $X$. No properness, quasi-compactness, Noetherian, finite-presentation, or flatness hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$ and $x\in U_n$. Choose an affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ containing $f(x)$. By the affine-cover definition of locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset f^{-1}(T)$ containing $x$, with $B$ a finite type $R$-algebra. Write $h:W\to T$ for the restriction of $f$. This uses a member of the cover supplied by that definition, rather than asserting finite type for arbitrary affine opens.

source.place: Tag 02FZ, affine reduction; Tag 01T2, label lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize, affine-cover condition (4)

proof.text: For every $y\in W$, put $s=f(y)$. The fibre homeomorphisms in [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identify the fibre of $h$ over $s$ with the open subspace $W\cap f^{-1}(s)$ of $f^{-1}(s)$, the underlying space of $X_s$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] identifies its local dimension at the point over $y$ with $\dim_{\widetilde y}X_s$. Apply [lem-sbc-affine-coordinate-fibre-dimension] to $h$: if $\mathfrak q_y\subset B$ corresponds to $y$ and $\mathfrak p_y$ is its contraction to $R$, this common dimension is $\dim_{\mathfrak q_y}(B/R)$, measured on $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p_y))$. The affine comparison writes the tensor factors in the opposite order; the swap $b\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes b$ has its own inverse and carries the kernel of $b\otimes a\mapsto\bar b\bar a$ to the same distinguished prime. Its spectrum homeomorphism carries open neighbourhoods and chains of irreducible closed subsets bijectively, so preserves the defining minimum of dimensions.

source.place: Tag 02FZ, affine reduction; Schemes Tag 01K1, label lemma-fibre-topological; Algebra Tag 00E6, label remark-fundamental-diagram; Topology Tag 0055, label definition-Krull, item (4)

proof.text: By [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], the local dimension at a point is a nonnegative integer or infinity. Since $x\in U_n$, it is therefore an integer $d$ with $0\leq d\leq n$. Step 2 identifies $\dim_{\mathfrak q_x}(B/R)=d$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-dimension-bounded-open-upstairs] to the finite type ring map $R\to B$ and this prime: there is an open $V\subset\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $\mathfrak q_x$ such that $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(B/R)\leq d$ for every $\mathfrak q\in V$. All its hypotheses are now in force; in particular no Noetherian or finite-presentation assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 00QH, label lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs; relative dimension defined in Tag 00QD, label definition-relative-dimension

proof.text: Pull $V$ back along the affine identification $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}B$ from [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the choice of $W$. This gives an open neighbourhood $N_x$ of $x$ in $W$, hence in $X$ because $W$ is open. For $y\in N_x$, steps 2 and 3 give $\dim_{\widetilde y}X_{f(y)}=\dim_{\mathfrak q_y}(B/R)\leq d\leq n$, so $N_x\subset U_n$. Consequently $U_n=\bigcup_{x\in U_n}N_x$ is open. If $U_n$ is empty this is the empty union, also open.
